title: DMS-MaPseq: Quantitative RNA structure profiling through mutation-based DMS detection
key_innovation: Compared with DMS-seq approaches based on reverse transcription stops, DMS-MaPseq uses error-prone reverse transcription to record DMS modifications as mutations, enabling quantitative structure mapping without truncation bias.

ppt_overview.title: How does DMS-MaPseq convert DMS modifications into sequencing signals?
ppt_overview.text: DMS-modified nucleotides are read through by a high-fidelity mutation-aware reverse transcriptase, which introduces mismatches into cDNA. These mutations are detected by deep sequencing to generate quantitative DMS reactivity profiles.

ppt_overview.title: Why does mutation-based detection improve DMS probing?
ppt_overview.captionTitle: Figure 2. TGIRT-based DMS-MaPseq improves signal quality.
ppt_overview.text: Compared with traditional RT-stop methods, mutation-based detection provides lower background and improved sensitivity for detecting DMS modifications.

ppt_overview.title: What structural information can DMS-MaPseq provide?
ppt_overview.alt: Global RNA structure analysis using DMS-MaPseq
ppt_overview.captionTitle: Figure 3. Global RNA structure analysis using DMS-MaPseq.
ppt_overview.text: DMS-MaPseq generates quantitative nucleotide-resolution structure profiles suitable for transcriptome-wide RNA folding analysis.
